To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NF-κ B protects developing NKT cell from TNF-α-mediated apoptosis, which is mediated by TNFR1, a death receptor.
NF-κB signaling protects developing NKT from TNFR1-induced death.
NF-κB integrates signals from the NKT cell TCR and TNFR1 to protect developing NKT cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the signal(s) integrated downstream of NF-κB during NKT cell development.
elucidating the role of NF-κB signal integration in the survival of developing NKT cells.
the identification of the signal(s) integrated downstream of NF-κB that protects NKT cells from TNF-α induced cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNFR1 is the death receptor that is integrated into the NF-κB survival pathway in developing NKT cell, and that TNFR1 signalling is a key upstream regulator of NKT cell survival and development.
NF-κ B protects NKT cell survival from TNF receptor 1-induced cell death.
the NF-κB pathway protects NKT cells from TNFα-induced death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NKT T cells are more sensitive to TNFR1 than to Fas and that TNFR1 is the major death signal that is integrated by NF- κB during NKT cell differentiation.
NF-κBs protect NKT cells from TNFR1-induced cell death, but not from other death signals.
the NF-κB pathway protects NKT cells from TNF-α induced death, which in turn is required for NKT cell development during thymopoiesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NF-κΒ is a key survival signal for NKT cells during their development.
the NKT cell survival signal integrated by NF- κB in developing Nekt cells is not derived from the TCR or the Fas receptor, but from the TNFR1.
the survival and development of NKT cells is regulated by NF-κBs, which integrate death signals emanating both from the TCR and from TNFR1.
